subject: Eval playbook & next steps — tool calling + JSON schema compliance
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Zhao <ethan.zhao@calliotech.com>, Priya Shah <priya@calliotech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Eval playbook & next steps — tool calling + JSON schema compliance

Hi Ethan / Priya,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good convo and very helpful context. Below is a concise post-call recap + proposed eval playbook so we can align on scope and next steps. I focused the plan on the three things you emphasized: structured-output reliability (JSON schema), safe tool/function calling to your LIMS, and cost/latency tradeoffs for production.

Recap (requirements we heard)
- Primary: reliably extract structured assay reports into a strict JSON schema for downstream analysis and audit.
- Tooling: model must call your LIMS API to fetch batch metadata and validate accession numbers.
- Failure mode handling: deterministic retry/backoff for transient LIMS failures, and a clear error envelope for manual review when model output fails schema validation.
- Quality bar: schema-pass rate >= 95% on production-like data; key-field accuracy (sample_id, concentration) >= 98%.
- Nonfunctional: p95 latency target <= 450ms for generation + tool call (for 256-token responses), cost threshold target to be discussed.

Initial recommended eval matrix (what we propose Redwood runs for POC)
- Candidate models: redwood-v2-13b-chat (full-fidelity), starling-7b-q4f (cost-optimized), redwood-instruct-3b (low-latency baseline).
- Benchmarks we will run: JSON-schema compliance test (5k samples from your anonymized corpus), hallucination spot checks (200 curated prompts), tool-call stability (1k concurrent simulated LIMS queries). Link to baseline runs: https://bench.redwood.ai/runs/5467-model-fit-calliope-aug2026
- Prompt sets: attached prompt_set_v1.jsonl — includes 50 prompt families we will use for schema/edge-case testing.

Evaluation deliverables (two-week POC suggested)
1) Week 1: model selection + schema compliance report (pass rates by field)
2) Week 2: tool-calling harness with retries + latency & cost summary; integration checklist for your engineering team

Operational constraints we propose
- Retry policy for tool calls (proto): exponential backoff with jitter — 200ms, 600ms, 1.8s (3 attempts), then return structured error envelope. We can tune per-endpoint.
- Error envelope format: {"status":"error","code":"LIMS_TIMEOUT","attempts":3,"raw_output":"<model output>"} — this will be wrapped in the response object so downstream systems can triage. (See attached example_schema_v2.json)
- JSON schema enforcement: Redwood's eval harness will run fast schema checks and classify failures by severity (critical missing fields vs. type mismatch) so we can quantify manual review load.

Next steps / asks from Calliotech
- Please share a small anonymized sample set (500 records) that represents your most common report shape. If you can upload to the Drive folder linked above that’s ideal.
- Confirm a security contact for SOC2/technical onboarding; Priya, can you share who owns that?
- Are there rate limits we should model for LIMS queries (QPS and auth method)?

Proposed timeline
- Kickoff technical POC: Mon Aug 24
- Interim readout (schema pass summary): Fri Aug 28
- Final POC review + next-phase SOW discussion: Wed Sep 2

I've looped in Laura (commercial lead) and Rishi (technical lead) — Rishi will follow up with the eval harness and retry policy specifics. If this plan looks good, I’ll send a calendar invite for Aug 24 kickoff.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference

Attachments: call_transcript_20260822.pdf (summary), prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompts), example_schema_v2.json

From: Ethan Zhao <ethan.zhao@calliotech.com>

Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval playbook & next steps — tool calling + JSON schema compliance

Alex — thanks for the clear recap. This is squarely what we need. A couple quick clarifying questions: 

1) When a model returns a near-miss (e.g., concentration unit mix-up: mg/L vs µg/mL), will your harness detect and surface that as a field-level accuracy issue vs a schema fail? We want to avoid too many "false positive" manual reviews.

2) Our LIMS team imposes a 200 QPS limit on public endpoints; we can provision a higher internal throttle for the POC if needed — we'll confirm yesterday. Auth is API key-based.

3) Latency: can you share an example p95 from the benchmark link for the redwood-v2-13b-chat run? We need to compare against internal SLAs.

Also, Priya — looping you to confirm the security point-of-contact.

—Ethan
CTO | Calliotech
ethan.zhao@calliotech.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Zhao <ethan.zhao@calliotech.com>, Priya Shah <priya@calliotech.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval playbook & next steps — tool calling + JSON schema compliance

Ethan / Alex / Priya — quick technical follow-up with specifics we will run during the POC so expectations are explicit.

Eval harness plan (concrete steps)
- Data ingestion: Redwood will run the attached prompt_set_v1.jsonl against three candidate model variants. We will sample 5k prompts total (stratified by assay type).
- Schema checks: use AJV-based validator with additional field-level checks (units normalization and numeric tolerance). Failures will be bucketed: critical_missing, type_mismatch, normalization_error. We will produce a per-field pass-rate CSV.
- Field accuracy: where numeric fields exist (concentration, dilution factor), compute absolute/relative error vs. ground truth; flag >1% relative error as an accuracy failure for key fields.

Tool calling & retry behavior
- Prototype retry policy (will be implemented in our connector): attempt 1 -> 200ms, attempt 2 -> 600ms, attempt 3 -> 1800ms with full jitter. On terminal failure the model response is replaced with the error envelope described in the schema.
- Idempotency: for endpoints that create resources, we'll require a client-supplied idempotency key; otherwise our harness will only perform read queries.

Observability
- We will emit trace spans to Datadog with tags: model_variant, schema_pass, tool_attempts, latency_ms. Sample trace link: https://app.datadog.com/trace/trace_id_sample (placeholder).

Benchmark numbers (quick snapshot from baseline run)
- redwood-v2-13b-chat: schema pass 96.1% (5k test set), p95 end-to-end latency = 420ms, token cost approx $0.018 per 1k tokens (hosted baseline).
- starling-7b-q4f: schema pass 92.4%, p95 = 310ms, cost ~40% lower.

We will include a short set of unit tests that exercises the most common edge-cases (missing fields, unit inconsistency, nested arrays). Those tests will be run nightly during the POC and results posted to the shared Drive.

If all good, I'll spin up the harness and post a first pass report by Fri Aug 28.

—Rishi
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Eval playbook & next steps — tool calling + JSON schema compliance

Ethan / Priya — great questions and thanks Rishi for the details. Confirming the plan and next steps below (mutual action plan):

Mutual action plan
- By Wed Aug 26: Calliotech uploads 500 anonymized sample reports to the Drive folder and confirms security contact.
- Mon Aug 24 (kickoff): Redwood begins harness runs (we'll throttle LIMS calls to 100 QPS until Calliotech confirms higher limits).
- Fri Aug 28: Redwood posts schema pass-rate report + initial latency/cost dashboard.
- Wed Sep 2: Joint review and decision point for SOW to continue to Dedicated/Private deployment.

Logistics: I’ll send calendar invites for the kickoff and final review. For the DocuSign SOW, Laura will send a preliminary SOW after Aug 28 contingent on results.

Ethan — to your question on near-misses: Rishi’s harness will report unit-normalization issues separately (normalization_error) so you can tune thresholds before they count as critical manual-review items. We can make that threshold configurable during the POC.

Thanks — looking forward to kickoff.
